Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 82, verse 1:

(p-449) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Infitar (The Cleaving).

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿When the sky is cleaved asunder﴾

That is: it is split open, as in Surah "al-Inshiqaq": ﴿When the sky splits open﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 1]. It has been said: out of awe of Allah.

It has also been said: due to the descent of the angels, as in His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And the day the sky will be split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down, descending﴾ [al-Furqan: 25].

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) has already discussed, in Surah "al-Shura", at the explanation of His statement, exalted is He, describing the horrors of the Resurrection: ﴿a Day that will make the children grey-haired﴾ ﴿the sky will be split open by it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 17-18].

Like the cleaving and the splitting open is the spreading apart (infiraj), as in His statement: ﴿And when the stars are obliterated﴾ ﴿and when the sky is opened up﴾ [al-Mursalat: 8-9].

**His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when the graves are overturned﴾**

That is, what is in them is scattered out (bu'thira man fīhā, "those in them are raised up"). As in His saying: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered out, and what is in the breasts is brought out?﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 9-10].

This wording indicates the speed of dispersal, like the scattering of grain from the palm, as in His saying: ﴿On the Day they emerge from the graves swiftly﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 43].

It has already been mentioned from the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon him and upon us, in Surat Qaf, at His saying: ﴿On the Day the earth will split open from them, rapidly﴾ [Qaf: 44].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 82, verse 5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Every soul will know what it has put forward and kept back﴾

(p-450) That is, every soul, as has already been explained in the surah "al-Takwir" (Surah 81).

Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on us and on him) discussed this matter in refuting the appearance of contradiction (idtirab) in the surah "al-Infitar" (Surah 82) here, at the same verse.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Dafʿ Iham al-Idtirab ʿan Ayat al-Kitab, "Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book"):

(p-435) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Infitar

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Every soul will know what it has put forward and kept back﴾.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse gives the impression that the one who will know on the Day of Resurrection what he has put forward and kept back is a single soul. But other verses have come indicating that every soul knows what it has put forward and kept back, such as His saying: ﴿There every soul will test what it has sent before﴾ [Yunus 10:30], and His saying: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird (deeds) to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find spread open﴾ [al-Isra' 17:13], and other verses besides these.

The answer is that what is meant by His saying "nafs" (a soul) is every soul. The indefinite noun, although it does not generalize except in the context of negation, a condition, or a favour (imtinan), as is established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul), the verified position is that it may sometimes convey generality through the indication of context, without negation, condition, or favour, such as His saying: ﴿Every soul will know﴾ [al-Takwir 81:14] in "al-Takwir" and "al-Infitar", and His saying: ﴿lest a soul be given up to destruction﴾, and His saying: ﴿lest a soul should say, "Oh, my regret"﴾. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 82, verse 7:

Allah's saying: ﴿Who created you, then proportioned you, then balanced you﴾ ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾

The explanation of this was given earlier by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, in surah "al-Kahf," at the words of Allah: ﴿His companion said to him while he was arguing with him, "Do you disbelieve in He who created you from dust, then from a drop [of semen], then proportioned you as a man?"﴾ [al-Kahf: 37], meaning: these are the stages of the human being in his creation.

Among what bears witness to the goodness of creation and the perfection of form is Allah's saying: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin: 4].

The difference of forms, despite their similarity, is indeed one of the signs of Allah, and it begins from the womb, as He said: ﴿He is the One who forms you in the wombs however He wills﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 6].

It was also mentioned earlier in surah "al-Hashr": ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾ [al-Hashr: 24].

And in the difference of forms, despite their resemblance, is among the greatest of the signs of Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 82, verse 10:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do.﴾

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) has already explained this in Surah Qaf, in discussing His words: ﴿When the two receivers receive, one seated on the right and one on the left. Not a word does he utter except that with him is an observer prepared.﴾ [Qaf: 17-18].

There, he referred to some of what came in Surah Maryam, in discussing His words: ﴿No! We will record what he says.﴾ [Maryam: 79].

He (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) also explained that this recording is to establish the proof against the human being, as in His words: ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find laid open. ﴾ ﴿"Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant."﴾ [Al-Isra: 13-14].

It has been said regarding ﴿ḥāfiẓīn﴾ (guardians): they guard the human body.

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) had also discussed this in Surah al-An'am, in discussing His words: ﴿And He sends over you guardians﴾ [Al-An'am: 61], citing His words: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before him and behind him, protecting him by the command of Allah﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 11].

Worth noting is that in describing the guardians here with these attributes, that they are guardians, noble, and knowing, all the qualities of fitness are gathered for them, not merely degrees of safeguarding, elevated rank, and knowledge of what they write.

It seems to be guidance for what those in authority should observe in appointing scribes and trustworthy persons.

For this reason they said: the judge should choose a trustworthy scribe, of good handwriting and understanding.

From this description it is known that no deed performed is confused for them, and that their being guardians means they lose nothing, even if it were the weight of an atom: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah: 7], and the verse continues.

Allah's statement: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾

That is: lasting bliss, as in His statement: ﴿Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and approval and gardens wherein is enduring pleasure. They will abide therein forever﴾ [At-Tawbah: 21-22].

The Exalted said: ﴿And they will not be absent from it.﴾

This is one of the proofs that the disbelievers abide forever in the Fire, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense, and they will not be absent from it.﴾ [Al-Infitar: 14–16].

Like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who followed will say, "If only we had another return, we would disassociate ourselves from them as they have disassociated from us." Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them. And they will never emerge from the Fire.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 167].

And this is generally the manner of the contrast between the two groups and their respective fates.

Then He explained that this is the Day of Recompense (yawm al-din), which is the Day of Requital, as was mentioned earlier in Surat al-Fatihah: ﴿Sovereign of the Day of Recompense.﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 4].

Then the Exalted explained the severity of the terror of that Day: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ [Al-Infitar: 17].

It has been mentioned earlier in: ﴿The Inevitable Reality. What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 1–2] (note: this is a cross-reference in the original commentary; the verse cited there is from Surat al-Haqqah).

And similar to it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The Striking Calamity. What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ [Al-Qari'ah: 1–2].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 82, verse 19:**

Allah's saying: ﴿On the Day when no soul will avail another soul in anything, and the command that Day belongs to Allah﴾.

That is, because of the severity of its terror and the weakness of the creatures, as was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother and his mother and his father﴾ [Abasa: 34–35], and His saying: ﴿For every one of them that Day, there will be a matter that occupies him﴾ [Abasa: 37].

And (it is supported) by the hadith of the intercession: "Every prophet will say, 'Myself, myself,' until it reaches the Prophet (ﷺ), who says, 'I am for it.'"

And the hadith of Fatimah: "Act. . . ."

And His saying: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], and what is similar to that.

As for His saying: ﴿and the command that Day belongs to Allah﴾, the apparent meaning of this verse is that the command is restricted to the stated time. But the command belongs to Allah on that Day, and it has been said that "that Day" (refers to the whole time), as in His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the command, before and after﴾ [al-Rum: 4].

And His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to Him belong the creation and the command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54], that is, He disposes of His creation as He wills by His command, and no one shares it with Him, just as no one shares His creation with Him.

For this reason He said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Say, "Indeed, the command, all of it, belongs to Allah"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 154].

And He said: ﴿You have no share in the command﴾ [Al 'Imran: 128], and what is similar to that.

However, the time-phrase (zarf) has come here for the sake of added emphasis, because in this world some people may have some commands, as in His saying: ﴿And enjoin your family to prayer﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132],

and His saying: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾ [al-Nisa': 59],

and His saying: ﴿So they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not right-guiding﴾ [Hud: 97]. All of these are, in reality, relative commands: ﴿And you will not will except that Allah wills﴾ [al-Insan: 30].

But on the Day of Resurrection, the true reality of the whole command and all sovereignty belong to Allah alone, the Exalted, as in His saying: ﴿"Whose is the dominion today?" "To Allah, the One, the Subduer"﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

So there is no command alongside His command, and no one can precede Him, not even with a word, except one whom the Most Merciful permits and who speaks rightly. This is like His saying: ﴿The dominion that Day belongs truly to the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan: 26], although in this world there are kings, as in the story of Joseph: ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me"﴾ [Yusuf: 50],

and in the story of al-Khidr and Musa: ﴿And there was behind them a king﴾ [al-Kahf: 79].

As for the Day of Resurrection, they will be as He said: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you﴾ [al-An'am: 94],

and like His saying: ﴿My authority has perished from me﴾ [al-Haqqah: 29]. Every authority and every dominion has gone, and the dominion that Day belongs to Allah, the One, the Subduer.
